- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% for the immediate follow-up period.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% deviation) and sentiment is neutral or positive, consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast toward historical mean of last 5–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >1.5% avg daily gain), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day lag.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values (neutral or bearish), model tends to lag behind true price; apply a 1–3 day lead correction to align with sentiment shift.
